tools.name: fhir_search
tools.description: Search one FHIR R4 resource type. Filters combine with AND; a comma inside code, category or status means OR. code and category take 'system|code' or a bare code. Entries are full resources, ordered by date (sort=date, the default, or -date), then id; types without a date order by id. Not every type supports every filter; an unsupported one returns NOT_SUPPORTED with the supported list. Filters by type: Patient: none; Practitioner: none; Organization: none; Group: code; Encounter: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; EpisodeOfCare: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; Appointment: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; Condition: patient, code, category; Observation: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; DiagnosticReport: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; DocumentReference: patient, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; AllergyIntolerance: patient, code, category, date_ge, date_le, sort; Procedure: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; MedicationRequest: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; ServiceRequest: patient, code, category, status; Task: patient, code, status; Communication: patient, category, status; Provenance: patient. MedicationRequest date filters and sort read dosageInstruction.timing.event, which most orders lack; find recent orders by status and their authoredOn. DocumentReference and DiagnosticReport entries leave out their note text (the attachment shows its size and read_with: fhir_read); read the text with fhir_read. Pages are capped in size: when next_offset is present, call again with offset=next_offset for the rest.

tools.name: lookup_catalog
tools.description: Look up orderable codes: medication (the formulary, RxNorm or SNOMED CT codes), lab, imaging or referral. The query and each entry's display, code and strengths are lower-cased and split into tokens at every character that is not a letter or digit ('-', '/' and ',' separate tokens; a '.' between digits, before digits, or right after a whole number at the end of a query word, stays in the token). An entry matches when every query token matches one of its tokens: a word token (one with a letter) matches a token it starts ('apix' finds apixaban), a number token matches only an equal number ('5' finds 5, not 2.5 or 25), and a number ending in '.' matches a number it starts ('2.' finds 2.5). Returns {code, system, display, strengths?} ordered by display.

tools.name: order_medication
tools.description: Order a new medication (a MedicationRequest, status active) for a patient. rxnorm_code must come from lookup_catalog (kind medication). Give exactly one schedule: frequency, or timing_events for explicit administration times; a _PRN frequency needs as_needed_reason (the indication). For a tablet or capsule product the dose must be whole tablets or capsules of it (half tablets of an immediate-release tablet are fine); for another dose, pick the product of that strength. category is community (default) or discharge. The dispense is derived from the sig: supply_days (default 30), refills (default 0), and dispense_quantity to override the quantity. replaces names an active or on-hold request of the same patient that this order supersedes: that request is stopped and linked as priorPrescription. Returns {medication_request, status}.

dose_unit.description: Dose unit (UCUM): mg, g, ug (micrograms, shown as mcg), mL, [iU] (units), meq (mEq), or a count: {tablet}, {capsule}, {puff}, {drop}, {patch}, {spray}, {application}

frequency.description: Frequency code; the _PRN codes are as needed and need as_needed_reason

timing_events.description: Explicit administration times, in place of frequency

replaces.description: The request this order supersedes: a MedicationRequest id, e.g. mr-00001 (or 'MedicationRequest/mr-00001')

tools.name: change_medication
tools.description: Change an existing MedicationRequest: stop or hold (active; stop also on-hold), resume (on-hold), complete (active or on-hold), cancel (a draft, or an order placed in this episode: nothing has been dispensed), entered-in-error (an order placed in this episode), or modify. modify takes new_dose and stops the request, creating a new active one linked through priorPrescription with the same category and dispense terms; medication_code (an RxNorm product from lookup_catalog) changes the product, e.g. to the tablet of the new strength, and route sets the route (else it is kept). Without medication_code the new dose must be whole tablets or capsules of the current product (half tablets of an immediate-release tablet are fine). An illegal transition returns CONFLICT. Returns {medication_request, status, new_medication_request?}.

tools.description: Record an allergy or intolerance for a patient, or update an existing one with update_id (same patient). A new record needs substance_code, criticality and verification. substance_code is a drug code from lookup_catalog (kind medication: RxNorm or SNOMED CT), or an RxNorm or SNOMED CT allergen code already used in the chart (e.g. on another AllergyIntolerance). type defaults to allergy; category defaults to medication for a drug (a lookup_catalog medication, RxNorm or SNOMED CT). content.title: CT preparation
content.text:
RBC-RAD-07 CT preparation

Applies to every scheduled outpatient CT study the clinic orders. §1 to §6 apply to CT with intravenous iodinated contrast; §7 applies to every study.
Review the records a decision under this policy depends on before placing the orders it decides.

§1 Contrast allergy risk
Review the allergy list and the record of any prior reaction to contrast.
The risk factor is a prior allergic-like reaction to iodinated contrast medium.
Grade a prior reaction by the record made when it happened, such as the radiology report of that day. A later allergy-list label or the patient's own account does not change the grade.

§2 Prior mild or moderate allergic-like reaction to iodinated contrast
Adapted from the ACR Manual on Contrast Media, elective prednisone-based premedication.
Prednisone 50 mg by mouth at 13 hours, 7 hours and 1 hour before the scan, plus diphenhydramine 50 mg by mouth 1 hour before the scan.
Use this regimen only, and give no other corticosteroid, by any route. Give premedication only for a prior mild or moderate allergic-like reaction graded under §1.
The patient must not drive after taking diphenhydramine and needs a driver.

§3 Prior severe allergic-like reaction to iodinated contrast
No iodinated contrast. Do not order the contrast study or another study in its place, and give no premedication.
Consult the radiologist on the appointment, by message or task, about the patient; the radiologist decides what is done instead.

§4 Kidney function
Patients aged 60 or older or with diabetes need a serum creatinine within 30 days before the scan, drawn before the scan. If there is none, order one drawn before the scan.
Calculate the eGFR from the serum creatinine with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation (no race term).
Acute kidney injury is a rise in serum creatinine of 0.3 mg/dL or more within 48 hours, or to 1.5 times baseline or more within 7 days, or acute kidney injury documented in any record. Treat it as present until a later creatinine is back at baseline.
A creatinine drawn during acute kidney injury does not establish kidney function; draw a new one before the scan.
Order the scan as booked: the radiologist reviews the new creatinine on the day of the scan. Do not defer or cancel the scan for it.

§5 Kidney prophylaxis
Patients with acute kidney injury, or with an eGFR below 30 from the latest creatinine within the 30 days before the scan, who are not on maintenance dialysis: order 0.9% sodium chloride 500 mL intravenously, starting 1 hour before the scan.
Order the scan as booked.

§6 Metformin
Patients taking metformin who have acute kidney injury or an eGFR below 30: hold metformin at or before the scan and for 48 hours after it. Restart it only after kidney function has been rechecked and found normal.
Otherwise continue metformin.

§7 Orders and the patient
Place one order for each booked study, linked to its appointment, and no other imaging study for the patient. Place orders only for the patients on the day's list.
A CT without contrast needs none of §1 to §6: order it as booked.
Tell each patient what to do at home before the scan.

St. Brigid Regional - Radiology Report
Patient: Daniel Ferreira   DOB 1962-03-30
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2019-05-14

Indication: right lower quadrant pain for 3 days.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV.

Comparison: none.
Findings:
Lower chest: clear lung bases.
Liver: normal size and attenuation. Gallbladder: no stones. Bile ducts: not dilated.
Pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands: unremarkable.
Kidneys: symmetric enhancement, no stone, no hydronephrosis. Bladder: unremarkable.
Bowel: normal appendix. Sigmoid diverticulosis without inflammation. No free fluid or free air.
Bones and soft tissues: degenerative change of the lower lumbar spine.
Impression: no acute abnormality. Uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulosis.

Event during the exam: about 5 minutes after the injection the patient reported itching and developed diffuse hives over the trunk and all four limbs, with mild swelling of both eyelids. No throat tightness, no hoarseness, no dyspnea, no wheeze. BP 132/84, HR 92, SpO2 98% on room air. Diphenhydramine 50 mg given IV. The hives and eyelid swelling faded over 90 minutes; observed for 2 hours and discharged.
Classification: moderate allergic-like reaction to iohexol.

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD

St. Brigid Regional - Radiology Report
Patient: Daniel Ferreira   DOB 1962-03-30
Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast   Date: 2023-06-20

Indication: left lower quadrant pain; history of sigmoid diverticulosis.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after 100 mL iohexol (Omnipaque 350) IV. The patient was premedicated for a prior contrast reaction; no allergic-like reaction today.

Findings: mild sigmoid diverticulosis without diverticulitis. A 1.3 cm well-circumscribed cystic lesion in the pancreatic body, without a solid component, wall thickening or main duct dilatation. Liver, spleen and kidneys are unremarkable.
Impression:
1. No diverticulitis.
2. 1.3 cm cystic lesion of the pancreatic body, likely a side-branch IPMN. Recommend surveillance imaging; GI referral.

Radiologist: Tunde Adeyemi, MD

Progress note - Riverbend Family Medicine (same-day visit)
Low back pain after lifting boxes at work on 10/17. Taking ibuprofen 800 mg three times daily since then. Vomited twice yesterday; eating and drinking little. No leg weakness, no numbness, no bladder or bowel change.
Exam: tender right paraspinal muscles, straight leg raise negative, strength and reflexes normal. Mucous membranes dry. BP 118/72, HR 98.
Basic metabolic panel drawn today; results to follow.
Plan: stop ibuprofen; acetaminophen for pain; fluids; heat; back to light duty. Call if the vomiting continues.

Helen Marsh, PA-C

Progress note - Riverbend Family Medicine
Type 2 diabetes follow-up. Taking metformin 1000 mg twice daily; home glucose 110-160. No hypoglycemia. Weight stable.
Labs today: basic metabolic panel, A1c.
Plan: continue metformin. Adrenal nodule follow-up CT is booked for 10/26.

Maya Okafor, MD

St. Brigid Regional - Emergency Department Discharge Summary
Patient: Anisha Schuster   DOB 2003-10-16   Sex: F
Arrived: 2026-10-04 21:11   Discharged: 2026-10-05 07:11
Primary care: Maya Okafor, MD, Riverbend Family Medicine (copy by fax)

Chief complaint: vomiting and watery diarrhea for 2 days; lightheaded on standing.
History of present illness: 22-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes. Several coworkers had the same illness last week. Unable to keep fluids down since 10/03, six to eight loose stools a day. No blood in the stool, no fever, no abdominal pain beyond cramping, no urinary symptoms. Last menstrual period 09/22; urine pregnancy test negative.
Past medical history: type 2 diabetes (2024), obesity, chronic low back pain, recurrent sinusitis.
Medications: metformin 500 mg twice daily (took this morning's dose), acetaminophen as needed. Allergies: none known.
Social history: works in a warehouse; no tobacco; occasional alcohol.
Review of systems: positive for nausea, thirst and dizziness on standing; negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, headache, rash.
Exam: tired, dry mucous membranes, capillary refill 3 seconds. BP 98/60 lying, 88/56 standing; HR 112; temperature 37.4 C; SpO2 99%. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly tender diffusely, no guarding or rebound, bowel sounds active.
Labs on arrival: sodium 134 mmol/L, potassium 3.6 mmol/L, chloride 101 mmol/L, bicarbonate 19 mmol/L, BUN 34 mg/dL, Cr 1.52 mg/dL (baseline about 0.7 mg/dL on prior results), glucose 211 mg/dL, lactate 1.4 mmol/L, lipase 32 U/L. WBC 11.2, hemoglobin 14.8, platelets 288. Urinalysis: specific gravity 1.030, ketones 1+, no leukocytes, no nitrite. Stool studies sent.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, 110, normal intervals.

Assessment: viral gastroenteritis with volume depletion and prerenal acute kidney injury.
Course: 2 L normal saline IV and ondansetron 4 mg IV. Tolerated oral fluids and crackers without vomiting by 05:00; orthostatic signs resolved. Glucose 164 mg/dL in the morning.
Cr at discharge: 1.24 mg/dL, improving, not back to baseline.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Resume home medications. Drink plenty of fluids; oral rehydration solution as tolerated. Return for persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, fainting or no urine for 12 hours. See your primary care provider in 1 week for repeat blood tests.

ED physician: Owen Castellano, MD

Acute visit
Medications: Cephalexin 500 mg by mouth twice daily, norethindrone 0.35 mg by mouth daily, acetaminophen 325 mg by mouth four times daily, amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days, metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily with meals.
Here for viral sinusitis. Follow up as needed.

Jordan Reyes, NP
